title: Last derivative of the noise operator
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and choose $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and a bit $b\in\{0,1\}$. The discrete derivative in the last coordinate of the noise operator applied to $f$, evaluated at the point obtained by appending $b$ to $x$, equals $\rho$ times the noise operator applied to the last-coordinate half-difference of $f$, evaluated at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional Boolean hypercube
replaced: Let $T_\rho$ denote Boolean noise with real correlation $\rho$, whose Fourier multiplier on a set of size $k$ is $\rho^k$. For $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, put $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, and $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and let $s_0=1$, $s_1=-1$. For every $x,b$, $D_n(T_\rho f)(x,b)=\rho(T_\rho d_f)(x)$, where $D_n$ is the last-coordinate half-difference.
